author: Mark Atwood
text:
Resolved via path 1 (document the contract). Path 2 (type-dispatch in MemoryBackend) intentionally not taken.

## What was added

1. New 'Per-type uniqueness contracts' section on `ChatBackend::create_object` rustdoc (backend.rs) naming the two types with non-id uniqueness invariants:
   - **ReadPosition** — (account_id, chat_id) MUST be enforced atomically with the create at the storage layer; handler pre-check is defense-in-depth only; race window between pre-check and create exists for two concurrent /set requests; production backends MUST close it.
   - **Chat with kind==Direct** — (account_id, contact_id) closed by handler-side optimistic-create-then-validate-with-rollback, so backends MAY but need not enforce a storage-level unique constraint.
   - Explicit note that the reference MemoryBackend does NOT enforce ReadPosition's constraint at the storage layer; it gets away with it via single-Mutex-per-call serialization, but a production backend with finer-grained locking MUST.

2. Tightened module-doc on position.rs to point at the trait contract section instead of stating 'backends must enforce' in isolation.

## Why path 2 was not taken

The bead's path 2 (add type-dispatch in MemoryBackend.create_object for TYPE_NAME == `ReadPosition::TYPE_NAME`) would make the reference impl a more faithful demonstration of the contract — but:

(a) MemoryBackend.create_object is generic-over-O. Type-string dispatch via O::TYPE_NAME comparison would special-case ReadPosition in a way that doesn't generalize to other types with similar constraints (a future type X with a different non-id uniqueness invariant would need its own special case). The kit's pattern is 'reference impl is loudly demonstration-only; production backend implements the real constraint' — see workspace AGENTS.md.

(b) The race window cannot actually fire against MemoryBackend: every create_object call acquires the same Mutex, so writes are serialized. Adding a scan-before-insert that mimics what a real DB unique constraint would do is theatre — it doesn't enable a new test, and the cost is per-create O(N) scan overhead that the reference impl doesn't need.

(c) The handler-side pre-check already closes the sequential / intra-batch duplicate case (committed in c5aac30, JMAP-x2gd.13). Path 1 closes the documentation gap; path 2 would close a race that the reference impl cannot expose.

## Gates

- cargo check -p jmap-chat-server --all-features: clean
- cargo clippy -p jmap-chat-server --all-features -- -D warnings: clean
- cargo test -p jmap-chat-server --all-features: 273 + integration tests passing
- RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc -p jmap-chat-server --no-deps --all-features: clean (rustdoc resolves the intra-doc links to handle_position_set and ChatBackend::create_object)
- cargo fmt --all: no changes

Diff: 2 files, +52 / -2 (pure rustdoc additions).

Closes JMAP-x2gd.101.
